question: What did Atlas change in the data-breach super-cap between our v1 form and their markup?
evidence: WILL NOT EXCEED FIVE TIMES (5X) THE ANNUAL SUBSCRIPTION FEES, THAT IS, TWO MILLION FOUR HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS ($2,400,000) | Required by NCUA vendor guidance per our CISO.

also.source: Email from Brightline's General Counsel with negotiating instructions (November 9, 2026)
also.evidence: Our form offers 2x the annual Subscription Fees ($960,000). We will not accept a super-cap above 3x ($1,440,000) under any circumstances.

note: Atlas's markup (v2, M. Sheridan, 2026-11-06) raises the Section 11.3 super-cap for breach of Section 8 (Security) or confidentiality involving Customer Data from two times (2x) the annual Subscription Fees ($960,000) in Brightline's v1 form to five times (5x) ($2,400,000), with the comment 'Required by NCUA vendor guidance per our CISO.' The general cap in 11.2 (fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the event) is unchanged. The client will not go above 3x ($1,440,000). The v1 wording is only in the earlier version of the same document.

question: Did Atlas change the uptime commitment in its markup of the MSA?
evidence: Brightline's monthly Availability commitment is ninety-nine point nine five percent (99.95%) in each calendar month | The service credits under Section 5.2 are without prejudice to Customer's other rights and remedies

also.source: SLA Schedule (Schedule 2) - Availability and service credits
also.evidence: Brightline will make the production environment of the Service available with a monthly Availability of at least 99.9% in each calendar month

also.source: Email from Atlas (Monica Sheridan) sending the markup (November 6, 2026)

note: Yes. Section 5.1 goes from 99.9% (v1) to 99.95% monthly Availability (comment: 'Atlas's board requires 99.95% for member-facing systems.'), and Section 5.3 no longer makes service credits Customer's sole and exclusive remedy: they are 'without prejudice to Customer's other rights and remedies'. The SLA Schedule (Schedule 2) was not marked up and still keys its credit table to 99.9% and repeats the sole-remedy wording.

question: How quickly does Brightline have to notify Atlas of a security incident? I've seen different numbers.
evidence: within twenty-four (24) hours after Brightline discovers the Security Incident

also.evidence: within seventy-two (72) hours after Brightline confirms the Personal Information Breach
Vendor shall notify Atlas of any Security Incident within forty-eight (48) hours after Vendor discovers it.

also.source: Email from Brightline's General Counsel with negotiating instructions (November 9, 2026)
also.evidence: We can live with 48 hours, which matches Atlas's own Information Security Addendum, but not 24.

note: Three different periods: (1) Brightline's v1 MSA (8.3) and its DPA (5.1): without undue delay and within 72 hours after Brightline confirms the incident / breach; (2) Atlas's markup of the MSA (v2, 8.3): 24 hours after discovery; (3) Atlas's own Information Security Addendum (6.1): 48 hours after discovery. Precedence clauses pull different ways (DPA 8.1: DPA prevails on Personal Information; ISA 11: the more protective provision prevails). The client will accept 48 hours, not 24.

question: Monica Sheridan's cover email says Atlas accepted our liability cap as drafted. Is that right?
evidence: WILL NOT EXCEED FIVE TIMES (5X) THE ANNUAL SUBSCRIPTION FEES, THAT IS, TWO MILLION FOUR HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS ($2,400,000)

also.source: Email from Atlas (Monica Sheridan) sending the markup (November 6, 2026)
also.evidence: we have accepted your liability cap as drafted and only tightened the uptime to 99.95%

note: No. The general cap in 11.2 is unchanged, but the markup raises the 11.3 data-breach super-cap from 2x ($960,000) to 5x ($2,400,000). The email ('only tightened the uptime to 99.95%') also leaves out the other changes: credits no longer the sole remedy (5.3), 24-hour incident notice from discovery (8.3), a new on-site audit right (8.6) and termination for convenience after 12 months on 90 days' notice with a pro-rata refund (10.4).

question: If Availability comes in at 99.3% in a month under the SLA Schedule, what service credit does Atlas get, in dollars?
source: SLA Schedule (Schedule 2) - Availability and service credits
evidence: < 99.5% but ≥ 99.0% | 10% | Based on Subscription Fees of $480,000 per year, the Monthly Fees are $40,000.
note: 99.3% falls in the '< 99.5% but ≥ 99.0%' band, so the credit is 10% of the Monthly Fees for that month: 10% x $40,000 ($480,000 / 12) = $4,000, well under the 25% monthly cap ($10,000). The credit is applied against the next invoice. (Atlas's 99.95% in the v2 MSA does not change the Schedule 2 table.)

question: Under the SLA Schedule, what credit applies if monthly availability is below 99.9% but at least 99.5%, and what is the most Atlas can get in credits in one month?
source: SLA Schedule (Schedule 2) - Availability and service credits
evidence: < 99.9% but ≥ 99.5% | 5% | The total service credits for any calendar month will not exceed 25% of the Monthly Fees for that month
note: 5% of the Monthly Fees for that month ($2,000 on Monthly Fees of $40,000). Credits are capped at 25% of the Monthly Fees in any month ($10,000), which is also the credit for Availability below 99.0%. The client's instructions are to cap credits at 15% if it accepts 99.95%.
